choices.textEs: Roosevelt usó la diplomacia y la negociación en América Latina mientras empleaba la fuerza militar exclusivamente contra las potencias europeas.

choices.text: Roosevelt applied a completely consistent and uniform approach — combining patient negotiation with credible military threats — equally and without distinction to all nations regardless of their relative power or geographic proximity to the United States.
choices.textEs: Roosevelt aplicó el mismo enfoque consistente — negociación respaldada por la fuerza militar — igualmente a todas las naciones independientemente de su poder o posición geográfica.

choices.text: Roosevelt deliberately avoided deploying or threatening military force in all circumstances, relying exclusively on economic sanctions, trade restrictions, and diplomatic isolation to achieve his foreign policy objectives throughout Latin America and Europe.
choices.textEs: Roosevelt evitó la fuerza militar por completo y dependió exclusivamente de sanciones económicas para lograr objetivos de política exterior tanto en América Latina como en Europa.

items.explanation: Roosevelt's foreign policy was strikingly asymmetric: in Latin America, he employed coercion, direct military intervention, and unilateral dictation of terms (the Roosevelt Corollary). In dealing with European great powers and Asian powers like Japan, he used mediation, multilateral diplomacy, and negotiation — most notably brokering the peace in the Russo-Japanese War (Portsmouth, 1905) for which he won the Nobel Peace Prize. This double standard reflected the power differential: Roosevelt respected the sovereignty of powerful nations while treating weaker Latin American nations as subordinate. Option B is the reverse of the historical record; Option C ignores the Latin American evidence; Option D misidentifies Roosevelt's approach.
items.explanationEs: La política exterior de Roosevelt era llamativamente asimétrica: en América Latina empleó coerción, intervención militar directa y dictado unilateral de términos (el Corolario Roosevelt). Al tratar con las grandes potencias europeas y asiáticas como Japón, utilizó mediación, diplomacia multilateral y negociación — notablemente mediando la paz en la guerra ruso-japonesa (Portsmouth, 1905). Este doble estándar reflejaba el diferencial de poder. La opción B invierte el registro histórico; la C ignora la evidencia latinoamericana; la D identifica incorrectamente el enfoque de Roosevelt.

UU. para estabilizar gobiernos extranjeros. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor la eficacia de este enfoque en comparación con la política del Gran Garrote de Roosevelt?

choices.text: Dollar Diplomacy was demonstrably more effective than Big Stick because it successfully achieved all of its stated U.S. strategic and commercial objectives in Latin America without requiring a single direct military intervention in any country.
choices.textEs: La Diplomacia del Dólar fue más efectiva que el Gran Garrote porque logró los objetivos de EE. UU. sin ninguna intervención militar.

choices.text: Dollar Diplomacy was entirely and immediately ineffective because financial incentives have historically never influenced political stability or governance quality in nations subject to external foreign financial pressure and oversight.

choices.text: Dollar Diplomacy failed primarily because American private banks were unwilling to participate in the risky, politically exposed overseas loan programs that Taft's strategy required, making the approach financially unworkable from the start.
choices.textEs: La Diplomacia del Dólar fracasó principalmente porque los bancos americanos no estaban dispuestos a participar en los préstamos que requería la estrategia de Taft.

choices.text: Dollar Diplomacy failed because financial entanglements required military protection when threatened, generating more interventions and greater anti-American resentment than the Big Stick policy it was meant to replace.
choices.textEs: La Diplomacia del Dólar fracasó en sus propios términos porque los enredos financieros requerían protección militar cuando eran amenazados, generando más intervenciones y mayor resentimiento anti-americano que la política del Gran Garrote que se suponía debía mejorar.

items.explanation: Dollar Diplomacy failed on its own terms: rather than reducing the need for military intervention, Taft's financial approach was followed by more military interventions in Nicaragua, not fewer. By encouraging American banks to take over foreign national debts, Taft created financial entanglements that required military protection when those loans were threatened by political instability. The policy also generated intense anti-American sentiment in Latin America, which would eventually contribute to the revolutionary movements that Dollar Diplomacy was supposedly designed to prevent. Roosevelt's Big Stick, while nakedly coercive, at least operated transparently. Options A and B present overly charitable or critical assessments without sufficient nuance; Option C misidentifies the primary flaw.
items.explanationEs: La Diplomacia del Dólar fracasó en sus propios términos: en lugar de reducir la necesidad de intervención militar, el enfoque financiero de Taft fue seguido por más intervenciones militares en Nicaragua, no menos. Al alentar a los bancos americanos a hacerse cargo de las deudas nacionales extranjeras, Taft creó enredos financieros que requerían protección militar. La opción A y B presentan evaluaciones demasiado benévolas o críticas sin suficiente matiz; la C identifica incorrectamente el defecto principal.

items.stem: Woodrow Wilson called his foreign policy approach 'Moral Diplomacy' and claimed it would be based on democratic values rather than financial interests or military power. Which of the following best evaluates the consistency between Wilson's stated principles and his actual policies in Latin America?
items.stemEs: Woodrow Wilson llamó a su enfoque de política exterior 'Diplomacia Moral' y afirmó que se basaría en valores democráticos en lugar de intereses financieros o poder militar. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor la coherencia entre los principios declarados de Wilson y sus políticas reales en América Latina?

choices.text: Wilson's Moral Diplomacy was fully consistent with his stated democratic principles because he successfully brought an end to all previous U.S. military interventions in Latin America, establishing a genuinely non-interventionist precedent.
choices.textEs: La Diplomacia Moral de Wilson fue completamente consistente con sus principios declarados porque puso fin exitosamente a todas las intervenciones militares de EE. UU. en América Latina.

choices.text: Wilson's actual record revealed a significant gap between moral rhetoric and practice: he intervened militarily in Latin America more frequently than his predecessors, showing that moral justifications provided new cover for the same interventionist patterns.
choices.textEs: El historial real de Wilson reveló una brecha significativa entre su retórica moral y su práctica: intervino militarmente en América Latina con más frecuencia que sus predecesores, demostrando que las justificaciones morales podían proporcionar nueva cobertura para los mismos patrones intervencionistas.

choices.text: Wilson's Moral Diplomacy was more effective than Big Stick or Dollar Diplomacy because moral arguments and democratic appeals successfully convinced Latin American governments to voluntarily align with U.S. political and commercial interests.
choices.textEs: La Diplomacia Moral de Wilson fue más efectiva que el Gran Garrote o la Diplomacia del Dólar porque los argumentos morales convencieron a los líderes latinoamericanos de alinearse voluntariamente con los intereses de EE. UU.

choices.text: Wilson's moral rhetoric was so persuasive in changing American public opinion that Congress consistently blocked him from conducting the military interventions in Latin America that his administration had planned and requested funding for.
choices.textEs: La retórica moral de Wilson tuvo tanto éxito en cambiar la opinión pública de EE. UU. que el Congreso le impidió llevar a cabo las intervenciones militares que había planeado.

items.explanation: Wilson's record in Latin America was deeply inconsistent with his stated moral principles. Despite condemning Dollar Diplomacy, Wilson intervened militarily more frequently than Taft or Roosevelt — sending troops to Mexico (twice), Haiti, and the Dominican Republic. His interventions in Haiti and the Dominican Republic were characterized by the same racial paternalism and suppression of self-determination that he criticized in others. Wilson's Moral Diplomacy demonstrated that high-minded rhetoric could coexist with interventionist practice, and indeed could provide new ideological cover for the same old patterns. Option A is factually inaccurate; Option C ignores the evidence; Option D creates an implausible causal claim.
items.explanationEs: El historial de Wilson en América Latina fue profundamente inconsistente con sus principios morales declarados. A pesar de condenar la Diplomacia del Dólar, Wilson intervino militarmente con más frecuencia que Taft o Roosevelt — enviando tropas a México (dos veces), Haití y la República Dominicana. La opción A es factualmente inexacta; la C ignora la evidencia; la D crea una afirmación causal implausible.

choices.text: The common imperial assumption was unique to Roosevelt's Big Stick approach; Taft's Dollar Diplomacy relied solely on economic incentives while Wilson's Moral Diplomacy genuinely respected Latin American political sovereignty and self-determination.
choices.textEs: El supuesto común solo estaba presente en la política de Roosevelt; Taft y Wilson genuinamente respetaron la soberanía latinoamericana.

choices.text: The common assumption was unique to Wilson's Moral Diplomacy, since he was the only president who explicitly claimed the authority to determine which Latin American governments were sufficiently legitimate and democratic to deserve U.S. recognition.
choices.textEs: El supuesto común solo estaba presente en la política de Wilson, ya que afirmó explícitamente el derecho de determinar qué gobiernos latinoamericanos eran moralmente legítimos.

choices.text: All three doctrines shared the assumption that the United States had the right to intervene in Latin American affairs when U.S. interests were threatened — the style of imperialism changed but the fundamental imperial relationship did not.
choices.textEs: Las tres doctrinas compartían el supuesto de que Estados Unidos tenía el derecho de intervenir en los asuntos latinoamericanos cuando los intereses de EE. UU. estaban amenazados, lo que significa que el estilo del imperialismo cambió pero la relación imperial fundamental permaneció constante.

choices.text: There was no common underlying assumption; each doctrine represented a genuinely different and incompatible understanding of U.S. rights and responsibilities in Latin America, making direct comparison between the three presidents misleading.
choices.textEs: No había un supuesto común; cada doctrina representaba una comprensión genuinamente diferente de los derechos de EE. UU. en América Latina.

items.explanation: Despite their stylistic differences — coercion (Roosevelt), financial leverage (Taft), moral suasion (Wilson) — all three approaches shared the common assumption that the United States had the right and responsibility to intervene in Latin American affairs when those affairs conflicted with U.S. interests. None of the three presidents accepted Latin American nations as genuinely sovereign equals. This common assumption explains why all three policies ultimately produced interventionist outcomes regardless of their stated philosophical differences. The implication is that the style of imperialism changed but the fundamental imperial relationship did not. Options A and B identify only one doctrine as sharing this assumption; Option D denies the common assumption exists.
items.explanationEs: A pesar de sus diferencias estilísticas — coerción (Roosevelt), apalancamiento financiero (Taft), persuasión moral (Wilson) — los tres enfoques compartían el supuesto común de que Estados Unidos tenía el derecho y la responsabilidad de intervenir en los asuntos latinoamericanos cuando esos asuntos conflictuaban con los intereses de EE. UU. Ninguno de los tres presidentes aceptó a las naciones latinoamericanas como genuinos iguales soberanos. Las opciones A y B solo identifican una doctrina como compartiendo este supuesto; la D niega que exista el supuesto común.

items.stem: The Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) presented Wilson with his greatest foreign policy challenge in Latin America. Wilson's intervention in Mexico, including the occupation of Veracruz (1914) and the Punitive Expedition against Pancho Villa (1916–1917), illustrates which of the following principles about Moral Diplomacy?
items.stemEs: La Revolución Mexicana (1910–1920) le presentó a Wilson su mayor desafío de política exterior en América Latina. La intervención de Wilson en México, incluyendo la ocupación de Veracruz (1914) y la Expedición Punitiva contra Pancho Villa (1916–1917), ilustra cuál de los siguientes principios sobre la Diplomacia Moral.

choices.text: Moral Diplomacy proved effective in Mexico because Wilson successfully promoted constitutional democratic governance by consistently supporting Venustiano Carranza's constitutional faction against all competing revolutionary factions.
choices.textEs: La Diplomacia Moral fue efectiva en México porque Wilson promovió exitosamente el gobierno democrático al apoyar la facción constitucionalista de la Revolución Mexicana.

choices.text: Moral Diplomacy was demonstrably superior to Big Stick Diplomacy because Wilson ultimately achieved his core objectives in Mexico without resorting to permanent military occupation of Mexican territory or annexation.
choices.textEs: La Diplomacia Moral fue superior al Gran Garrote porque Wilson logró los mismos objetivos que Roosevelt hubiera logrado pero sin ocupación militar permanente.

choices.text: Moral Diplomacy proved that a genuinely non-interventionist foreign policy was achievable when consistently guided by democratic principles rather than the commercial and strategic economic interests that had motivated previous presidents.
choices.textEs: La Diplomacia Moral demostró que era posible lograr una política exterior no intervencionista cuando se guiaba por principios democráticos en lugar de intereses económicos.

choices.text: Moral Diplomacy in practice authorized intervention whenever a foreign government failed Wilson's moral standards, making it an interventionist doctrine with ideological justification rather than a genuine departure from Big Stick or Dollar Diplomacy.
choices.textEs: La Diplomacia Moral en la práctica autorizó la intervención siempre que un gobierno extranjero no cumpliera con los estándares morales de Wilson, lo que la convirtió en una doctrina intervencionista con justificación ideológica en lugar de una verdadera ruptura con el Gran Garrote o la Diplomacia del Dólar.

items.explanation: Wilson's interventions in Mexico illustrate a fundamental problem with Moral Diplomacy: when Wilson decided that a Mexican government was not legitimate by his moral standards (as with Huerta), he felt justified in intervening militarily to change it — exactly the kind of unilateral intervention he had criticized. Moreover, the Punitive Expedition against Villa showed that military power remained the instrument of last resort even under a morally framed foreign policy. The Mexico case demonstrates that Moral Diplomacy was not a non-interventionist doctrine but rather an interventionist one with a different rhetorical justification. Options A and B are too charitable; Option C confuses Moral Diplomacy with non-interventionism.
items.explanationEs: Las intervenciones de Wilson en México ilustran un problema fundamental con la Diplomacia Moral: cuando Wilson decidió que un gobierno mexicano no era legítimo según sus estándares morales, se sintió justificado para intervenir militarmente para cambiarlo. Además, la Expedición Punitiva contra Villa demostró que el poder militar seguía siendo el instrumento de último recurso incluso bajo una política exterior enmarcada moralmente. Las opciones A y B son demasiado benévolas; la C confunde la Diplomacia Moral con el no intervencionismo.

UU. en América Latina en comparación con sus predecesores. ¿Cuál de las siguientes conclusiones está mejor respaldada por este hallazgo?

choices.text: The specific diplomatic doctrine mattered less than the structural factors — economic interests, Panama Canal security
choices.textEs: La doctrina diplomática específica importó menos que los factores estructurales — intereses económicos, seguridad del Canal de Panamá y hegemonía hemisférica — que impulsaron la intervención independientemente del marco filosófico que los presidentes usaran para justificarla.

choices.text: Wilson's Moral Diplomacy was the most effective at increasing U.S. power in Latin America, which is why his administration produced the most interventions.
choices.textEs: La Diplomacia Moral de Wilson fue la más efectiva para aumentar el poder de EE. UU. en América Latina, razón por la cual su administración produjo la mayor cantidad de intervenciones.

choices.text: Dollar Diplomacy caused more instability than Big Stick or Moral Diplomacy, explaining why all three presidencies saw increased intervention.
choices.textEs: La Diplomacia del Dólar causó más inestabilidad que el Gran Garrote o la Diplomacia Moral, lo que explica por qué los tres presidentes vieron un aumento de las intervenciones.

choices.text: The three doctrines were fundamentally the same policy, and historians who distinguish between them are making a category error.
choices.textEs: Las tres doctrinas eran fundamentalmente la misma política, y los historiadores que distinguen entre ellas están cometiendo un error de categoría.

items.explanation: If all three presidents, despite different stated philosophies, increased military intervention in Latin America, the most defensible conclusion is that the specific diplomatic doctrine mattered less than the structural factors that drove intervention: U.S. economic interests in the region, the need to protect the Panama Canal, and the logic of hemispheric hegemony embedded in the Monroe Doctrine/Roosevelt Corollary framework. The different doctrines were different rhetorical strategies layered over a consistent interventionist practice driven by structural interests. This is a more sophisticated conclusion than attributing outcomes to one president's philosophy. Options B, C, and D make unjustifiably specific causal claims not supported by the comparative evidence.
items.explanationEs: Si los tres presidentes, a pesar de sus diferentes filosofías declaradas, aumentaron la intervención militar en América Latina, la conclusión más defendible es que la doctrina diplomática específica importó menos que los factores estructurales que impulsaron la intervención: los intereses económicos de EE. UU. en la región, la necesidad de proteger el Canal de Panamá y la lógica de hegemonía hemisférica. Las opciones B, C y D hacen afirmaciones causales injustificadamente específicas.

items.stemEs: La Diplomacia del Dólar de Taft tenía como objetivo reemplazar la intervención militar con influencia económica. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor el supuesto subyacente que hizo plausible esta sustitución para Taft?

choices.text: Taft assumed that Latin American governments would willingly submit to comprehensive U.S. financial supervision and auditing in exchange for guaranteed American military protection against internal revolt and external creditor pressure.
choices.textEs: Taft asumió que los gobiernos latinoamericanos se someterían voluntariamente al control financiero de EE. UU. a cambio de protección militar.

choices.text: Taft assumed that economic stability was the primary driver of political stability, and that American financial penetration would give Latin American governments the resources and incentives to maintain order and repay debts.
choices.textEs: Taft asumió que la estabilidad económica era el principal motor de la estabilidad política, y que la penetración financiera americana daría a los gobiernos latinoamericanos los recursos e incentivos para mantener el orden sin requerir aplicación militar.

choices.text: Taft assumed that American private banks would willingly absorb all financial risks in Latin American loan markets without any government backing, interest guarantees, or diplomatic pressure to participate.
choices.textEs: Taft asumió que los bancos privados americanos absorberían voluntariamente todos los riesgos financieros sin ninguna garantía de apoyo del gobierno de EE. UU.

choices.text: Taft assumed that the consistent expansion of free-market capitalism through American investment would naturally and automatically produce stable democratic governance throughout Latin America over a generation.
choices.textEs: Taft asumió que el capitalismo de libre mercado produciría naturalmente un gobierno democrático en América Latina con el tiempo.

items.explanation: Taft's logic rested on a specific assumption: that political stability in Latin America was primarily a product of economic stability, and that if American investment and banking replaced European creditors, U.S. financial interests would give Latin American governments both the resources and the incentive to maintain order. This is essentially a modernization theory argument — that economic development produces political stability. The assumption proved flawed because political instability in Latin America had deeper roots in inequality, land tenure, and nationalist politics that financial arrangements could not address. Option A misidentifies the assumption; Option C describes the mechanism, not the assumption; Option D applies a later-era concept.
items.explanationEs: La lógica de Taft descansaba en un supuesto específico: que la estabilidad política en América Latina era principalmente un producto de la estabilidad económica, y que si la inversión y la banca americana reemplazaban a los acreedores europeos, los intereses financieros de EE. UU. darían a los gobiernos latinoamericanos tanto los recursos como el incentivo para mantener el orden. El supuesto resultó defectuoso porque la inestabilidad política tenía raíces más profundas. La opción A identifica incorrectamente el supuesto; la C describe el mecanismo; la D aplica un concepto de una era posterior.

items.stem: Roosevelt's negotiation of the peace treaty ending the Russo-Japanese War (Treaty of Portsmouth, 1905) is often cited as an example of Big Stick diplomacy applied on a global scale. Which of the following best evaluates what this negotiation reveals about the limits of Big Stick diplomacy as a global strategy?
items.stemEs: La negociación de Roosevelt del tratado de paz que puso fin a la guerra ruso-japonesa (Tratado de Portsmouth, 1905) se cita frecuentemente como un ejemplo de la diplomacia del Gran Garrote aplicada a escala global. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor qué revela esta negociación sobre los límites de la diplomacia del Gran Garrote como estrategia global?

choices.text: The Portsmouth negotiation conclusively proves that Big Stick diplomacy could be applied with equal effectiveness universally — to both great powers and small nations — making it the optimal instrument of American diplomacy in all international contexts.
choices.textEs: La negociación de Portsmouth demuestra que la diplomacia del Gran Garrote podría aplicarse universalmente con igual efectividad tanto a las grandes potencias como a las naciones más pequeñas.

choices.text: The Portsmouth negotiation proves that direct military force, rather than diplomatic mediation, was ultimately the decisive factor in Roosevelt's success as a global statesman dealing with major European and Asian powers.
choices.textEs: La negociación de Portsmouth demuestra que la fuerza militar fue el factor decisivo en el éxito de Roosevelt como diplomático global.

choices.text: The Portsmouth negotiation clearly demonstrates that all foreign policy situations and international crises respond equally well to the same diplomatic approach and strategic toolkit, regardless of the power differential between the parties involved.
choices.textEs: La negociación de Portsmouth muestra que todas las situaciones de política exterior responden igualmente bien al mismo enfoque diplomático, independientemente de los diferenciales de poder.

choices.text: The Portsmouth negotiation reveals that Big Stick diplomacy required genuine mediation when applied to great powers, working only where U.S. power superiority allowed coercive pressure rather than negotiated compromise.
choices.textEs: La negociación de Portsmouth revela que la diplomacia del Gran Garrote solo fue efectiva en contextos de superioridad de poder de EE. UU., y que tratar con grandes potencias requirió mediación y negociación genuinas en lugar de amenazas coercitivas.

items.explanation: The Portsmouth negotiation reveals an important limit of Big Stick diplomacy: the 'stick' only works when you have something the other party fears. With Russia and Japan, Roosevelt's leverage was limited — he could not realistically threaten either great power militarily. Instead, he succeeded through mediation (offering to broker peace), which both exhausted powers found attractive. This demonstrates that Big Stick worked in Latin America because of the power asymmetry — the U.S. could credibly threaten smaller nations — but required genuinely different diplomatic tools when dealing with great powers. Options A and B mischaracterize the Portsmouth negotiation; Option C ignores the power differential that made the difference.
items.explanationEs: La negociación de Portsmouth revela un límite importante de la diplomacia del Gran Garrote: el 'garrote' solo funciona cuando se tiene algo que la otra parte teme. Con Rusia y Japón, el apalancamiento de Roosevelt era limitado — no podía amenazar militarmente a ninguna gran potencia. En cambio, tuvo éxito a través de la mediación. Esto demuestra que el Gran Garrote funcionó en América Latina debido a la asimetría de poder, pero requirió herramientas diplomáticas genuinamente diferentes al tratar con grandes potencias. Las opciones A y B caracterizan incorrectamente la negociación de Portsmouth; la C ignora el diferencial de poder.

items.stem: Wilson's Moral Diplomacy asserted that the United States would only recognize governments that were 'just' by democratic standards. Which of the following best evaluates the precedent this principle set for future U.S. foreign policy?
items.stemEs: La Diplomacia Moral de Wilson afirmó que Estados Unidos solo reconocería gobiernos que fueran 'justos' según estándares democráticos. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor el precedente que este principio estableció para la política exterior futura de EE. UU.?

choices.text: It established the precedent that the U.S. could judge the domestic legitimacy of foreign governments and condition recognition on meeting U.S.-defined democratic standards
choices.textEs: Estableció el precedente de que EE. UU. podía juzgar la legitimidad interna de los gobiernos extranjeros y condicionar el reconocimiento al cumplimiento de los estándares democráticos definidos por EE. UU. — un principio que reaparecería como justificación para la intervención durante el siglo XX pero que se aplicó selectivamente según la conveniencia estratégica.

choices.text: It established the precedent that the United States would only engage in foreign trade with nations that had freely elected governments.
choices.textEs: Estableció el precedente de que Estados Unidos solo se involucraría en comercio exterior con naciones que tuvieran gobiernos libremente elegidos.

choices.text: It had no lasting precedent because Wilson's principle was immediately abandoned by his successors and never applied after 1921.
choices.textEs: No tuvo precedente duradero porque el principio de Wilson fue inmediatamente abandonado por sus sucesores y nunca se aplicó después de 1921.

choices.text: It established the precedent that the United States would refrain from intervention in other nations' affairs as long as those nations maintained democratic institutions.
choices.textEs: Estableció el precedente de que Estados Unidos se abstendría de intervenir en los asuntos de otras naciones siempre que esas naciones mantuvieran instituciones democráticas.

items.explanation: Wilson's principle that the U.S. would recognize only democratically legitimate governments created a precedent for the use of recognition policy as a foreign policy tool — and, more broadly, for the idea that the U.S. had the right to judge the domestic governance of other nations and act accordingly. This would recur throughout the 20th century as a justification for interventions: if a government fails to meet U.S.-defined standards of legitimacy, the U.S. can justify withholding recognition or intervening. However, the principle was also dangerously selective — applied inconsistently based on strategic convenience rather than genuine democratic values. Option B applies to a different context; Options C and D mischaracterize the precedent's implications.
items.explanationEs: El principio de Wilson de que EE. UU. tenía el derecho de juzgar la gobernanza interna de otras naciones. items.stem: A student argues: 'Roosevelt, Taft, and Wilson all had fundamentally different visions of America's role in the world.' A second student counters: 'All three shared a fundamentally imperial vision; they only differed in method.' Which of the following best evaluates which argument is better supported by the historical evidence?
items.stemEs: Un estudiante argumenta: 'Roosevelt, Taft y Wilson tenían visiones fundamentalmente diferentes del papel de América en el mundo.' Un segundo estudiante contraargumenta: 'Los tres compartían una visión fundamentalmente imperial; solo diferían en el método.' ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor qué argumento está mejor respaldado por la evidencia histórica?

choices.text: The first student is entirely correct; the philosophical and methodological differences between the three doctrines were so fundamental that grouping them all as versions of American imperialism is analytically misleading and historically inaccurate.
choices.textEs: El primer estudiante tiene completamente la razón; las tres doctrinas representaban visiones tan fundamentalmente diferentes que compararlas como versiones del imperialismo es engañoso.

choices.text: The first student is mostly correct because the genuine philosophical differences between the three doctrines produced radically different outcomes in Latin American political stability, economic development, and attitudes toward the United States.
choices.textEs: El primer estudiante tiene mayormente razón porque las diferencias filosóficas entre las tres doctrinas produjeron resultados radicalmente diferentes en América Latina.

choices.text: The second student's argument is better supported: all three presidents operated within a shared imperial framework accepting U.S. rights to manage Latin American affairs, while differences in method were real but secondary to that foundational agreement.
choices.textEs: El argumento del segundo estudiante está mejor respaldado porque los tres presidentes operaron dentro de un marco imperial compartido — aceptando los derechos de EE. UU. de gestionar los asuntos latinoamericanos — mientras que las diferencias en el método eran reales pero secundarias a este acuerdo fundacional.

choices.text: Neither student's argument can be adequately evaluated because the available historical evidence about the specific intentions, decisions, and outcomes of all three presidential doctrines is simply insufficient to draw any comparative conclusions.
choices.textEs: El argumento de ninguno de los dos estudiantes puede evaluarse porque la evidencia es insuficiente para sacar conclusiones sobre las tres doctrinas.

items.explanation: The historical evidence better supports the second student's argument, but with nuance. All three presidents accepted the premise that the United States had the right — and responsibility — to manage Latin American affairs, protect U.S. strategic and economic interests through force if necessary, and evaluate foreign governments by U.S. standards. The differences were real — different rhetorical frameworks, different preferred instruments, different levels of willingness to use direct military force — but they operated within a shared imperial framework. The first student captures the genuine differences in approach; the second captures the shared underlying assumptions. A sophisticated assessment acknowledges both the genuine differences and the shared foundation. Option A dismisses the differences as irrelevant; Option B gives them too much weight; Option D evades the evaluative question.
items.explanationEs: La evidencia histórica respalda mejor el argumento del segundo estudiante, pero con matices. Los tres presidentes aceptaron la premisa de que EE. UU. tenía el derecho y la responsabilidad de gestionar los asuntos latinoamericanos. Las diferencias eran reales — diferentes marcos retóricos, diferentes instrumentos preferidos — pero operaban dentro de un marco imperial compartido. La opción A descarta las diferencias como irrelevantes; la B les da demasiado peso; la D evade la pregunta evaluativa.

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from President Theodore Roosevelt's Annual Message to Congress, December 7, 1903, regarding the Panama Canal (Bryan, William Jennings, ed., Republic or Empire (1899), public domain — public domain):

"No single great material work which remains to be undertaken on this continent is of such consequence to the American people as the building of a canal across the Isthmus connecting North and South America... The canal will benefit us commercially chiefly by reducing the distance and therefore the time and cost of transporting freight between the Atlantic and Pacific coasts... The canal is emphatically a work which it is for the interest of the entire civilized world to see undertaken and completed."

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of U.S. foreign policy from 1898 to 1914, construct a written argument that evaluates how the acquisition and construction of the Panama Canal represented both a triumph of American engineering ambition and a controversial exercise of imperial power. Your argument must include a specific claim, at least two pieces of evidence addressing both the strategic/economic benefits and the political controversy surrounding U.S. actions in Panama, and reasoning that connects the canal's construction to the broader pattern of American foreign policy in this era.
items.stemEs:
Lea el siguiente fragmento del Mensaje Anual al Congreso del Presidente Theodore Roosevelt, 7 de diciembre de 1903, sobre el Canal de Panamá (Registro del Congreso de EE. UU. — dominio público):

"Ninguna gran obra material que quede por emprender en este continente tiene tanta consecuencia para el pueblo americano como la construcción de un canal a través del Istmo que conecta América del Norte y del Sur... El canal nos beneficiará comercialmente principalmente reduciendo la distancia y por lo tanto el tiempo y el costo del transporte de carga entre las costas del Atlántico y el Pacífico... El canal es enfáticamente una obra que es del interés de todo el mundo civilizado ver emprendida y completada."

Usando este fragmento y su conocimiento de la política exterior de EE. UU. de 1898 a 1914, construya un argumento escrito que evalúe cómo la adquisición y construcción del Canal de Panamá representó tanto un triunfo de la ambición ingenieril estadounidense como un ejercicio controvertido del poder imperial. Su argumento debe incluir una afirmación específica, al menos dos evidencias que aborden tanto los beneficios estratégicos/económicos como la controversia política en torno a las acciones de EE. UU. en Panamá, y un razonamiento que conecte la construcción del canal con el patrón más amplio de la política exterior estadounidense en esta era.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring response makes a specific claim — for example: 'While the Panama Canal delivered undeniable strategic and commercial benefits to the United States, its construction required the U.S. to engineer a Panamanian revolution and override Colombian sovereignty, establishing a pattern of interventionism that would define U.S.-Latin American relations for decades.' Evidence should include: (1) U.S. support for the Panamanian independence movement from Colombia in November 1903 — Roosevelt sent warships to prevent Colombia from suppressing the revolt; (2) the Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty (1903) — newly independent Panama granted the U.S. a 10-mile-wide Canal Zone in perpetuity in exchange for $10 million plus annual payments; (3) strategic benefits: the canal reduced travel between New York and San Francisco from 14,000 miles around Cape Horn to 5,200 miles, transforming U.S. naval power projection consistent with Mahan; (4) diplomatic controversy: Colombia was offered $25 million in compensation only in 1921, and the U.S. did not cede the Canal Zone until the Torrijos-Carter Treaties (1977/1999). Reasoning should connect Roosevelt's framing ('civilized world' benefit) to his paternalistic view of Latin American sovereignty, previewing the Roosevelt Corollary.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an strategic argument that connects US.22, US.23 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Specific, defensible claim addressing both triumph and imperial controversy. Two or more specific pieces of evidence (e.g., 1903 revolution, Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty, strategic mileage reduction, Colombian compensation). Reasoning explicitly connects canal construction to the larger pattern of Big Stick diplomacy and previews or references the Roosevelt Corollary. Roosevelt's language in the excerpt is analyzed, not just quoted.
3 - Proficient: Clear claim. Two relevant pieces of evidence. Reasoning connects the canal to U.S. foreign policy patterns but may not fully develop the imperial-controversy dimension.
2 - Developing: Claim present but vague. One specific piece of evidence. Limited reasoning; may describe the canal without evaluating the political controversy.
1 - Beginning: No clear claim. Vague or absent evidence. Response mainly describes canal construction without analysis.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Colombian rejection of Hay-Herrán Treaty (1903); U.S.-backed Panamanian revolution (November 1903); Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty (1903); 10-mile Canal Zone in perpetuity; strategic distance reduction (Cape Horn vs. canal route); connection to Mahan's sea-power thesis; Roosevelt Corollary (1904) as follow-on policy; Colombian apology payment (1921).

El razonamiento conecta explícitamente la construcción del canal con el patrón más amplio de la diplomacia del Gran Garrote y anticipa o referencia el Corolario Roosevelt. Se analiza el lenguaje de Roosevelt en el fragmento.

(noviembre 1903); Tratado Hay-Bunau-Varilla (1903); Zona del Canal de 10 millas a perpetuidad; reducción de distancia estratégica; conexión con la tesis del poder naval de Mahan; Corolario Roosevelt (1904); pago de compensación a Colombia (1921).

choices.text: Mexico's declaration of war against the United States
The U.S. decision to enter World War I against Germany
The signing of the Treaty of Versailles
The passage of the Neutrality Acts of the 1930s

items.explanation: The Zimmermann Telegram, in which Germany proposed a Mexican alliance and the recovery of territory lost to the United States, was published in early 1917 and hardened American opinion toward the war Congress declared that April. Choice A is wrong because Mexico declined the proposal and did not declare war. Choice C is wrong because the Treaty of Versailles came in 1919, after the fighting ended. Together with unrestricted submarine warfare, the telegram made continued neutrality untenable.

choices.text: Roosevelt's 'Big Stick' diplomacy combined military readiness with assertive action, as seen in his support for Panamanian independence and unilateral canal construction
Roosevelt preferred diplomatic negotiation over action, as shown by his patient 20-year effort to gain permission from Colombia
The canal project demonstrated Roosevelt's isolationist beliefs and reluctance to engage in foreign affairs

items.explanation: The Panama Canal epitomized Roosevelt's 'Big Stick' diplomacy: he supported Panama's secession from Colombia when Colombia rejected a canal treaty, quickly recognized the new nation, secured canal rights, and deployed American engineers and military resources. This assertive, action-oriented approach defined Roosevelt's foreign policy and expanded American influence throughout the Western Hemisphere via the Roosevelt Corollary.
items.explanationEs: El canal ejemplificó la diplomacia del 'Gran Garrote' de Roosevelt: acción asertiva combinada con preparación militar.
